title: O, Draw Me, Father, After Thee
description: O, Draw Me, Father, After Thee in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 222, “Aspiration”, where the book credits them to a Moravian source.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, Draw me, Fa-ther, af-ter Thee! So shall I run and nev-er tire; With gra-cious words still com-fort me; Be Thou my hope, my sole de-sire; Free me from ev-ery weight; nor fear Nor sin can come, if Thou art near.

lines: O, Draw me, Father, after Thee!
So shall I run and never tire;
With gracious words still comfort me;
Be Thou my hope, my sole desire;
Free me from every weight; nor fear
Nor sin can come, if Thou art near.
Ere knew this beating heart to move,
Ever with me may they abide,
And close me in on every side.
In suffering be Thy love my peace;
In weakness be Thy love my power;
And when the storms of life shall cease,
O Father! in my latest hour,
In death as life, be Thou my guide,
And draw me closer to Thy side.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
